data.narrative: Completed Module 4 learning debugging toolbox - chose manual profiling strategy over APM for cost efficiency and no overhead, used memory profiler to find connection leak (fixed with finally block), query logging to find N+1 pattern (fixed with joinedload), CPU profiler to identify ReDoS vulnerability (fixed with URL parser and input length limit).

dimension_scores.observation: Formed hypotheses for performance issues before profiling - memory leak on error path, N+1 query pattern from dependency update, ReDoS from regex backtracking on repeating characters. Used tools to confirm each hypothesis.
dimension_scores.evidence: module4_cpu_spike_bug.md documents three hypotheses for CPU spike issue

dimension_scores.observation: Used query logging to identify N+1 pattern - enabled SQL logging to see actual queries ORM generated, revealing 51 queries instead of expected 1. This showed runtime behavior code reading would miss.
dimension_scores.evidence: module4_performance_bugs.md describes query logging revealing 51 queries

dimension_scores.observation: Reproduced CPU spike bug with specific URL containing repeating characters, used profiler to identify function consuming CPU. Reproduced memory leak with 2000 requests showing growing memory usage.
dimension_scores.evidence: module4_cpu_spike_bug.md describes reproduction with malicious URL

dimension_scores.observation: Module 4 did not exercise communication under pressure - this dimension is introduced in Module 05 for incident response. Set baseline score as no evidence yet.
dimension_scores.evidence: No incident communication performed in Module 4 - focused on profiling technique.

dimension_scores.observation: Traced memory leak to missing finally block (systemic: cleanup not in error path), N+1 query to dependency update changing ORM defaults (systemic: silent config changes), ReDoS to vulnerable regex pattern (systemic: regex backtracking vulnerability).
dimension_scores.evidence: module4_performance_bugs.md explains dependency update as root cause. module4_redos_fix.md explains catastrophic backtracking mechanism.

dimension_scores.observation: Module 4 did not exercise postmortem quality - this dimension is introduced in Module 07. Set baseline score as no evidence yet.
dimension_scores.evidence: No postmortem analysis performed in Module 4 - focused on profiling technique.

strengths: Chose manual profiling strategy for cost efficiency and no overhead
Used profilers to identify runtime behavior code reading would miss
Fixed memory leak with finally block ensuring cleanup on error paths
Replaced regex with URL parser to eliminate ReDoS vulnerability
data.recommendation: Continue to Module 05 to develop communication under pressure skills - delivering clear, honest status updates during active incidents to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

public_evidence.student_action: Identified catastrophic backtracking in regex validation using CPU profiler, replaced regex with built-in URL parser (urllib.parse), added 2048 character input length limit as defense in depth. Verified fix reduces response time from 47-52 seconds to milliseconds with normal CPU usage.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Replaced regex URL validation with urllib.parse.urlparse() in Python, added MAX_URL_LENGTH = 2048 validation before parsing
public_evidence.ability: Profiling and fixing performance vulnerabilities including ReDoS
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates ability to use CPU profilers to identify performance bottlenecks, understand catastrophic backtracking vulnerabilities, and implement defensive programming with standard libraries and input validation

module4_performance_bugs.md describes heap snapshots showing memory growth
module4_redos_fix.md explains catastrophic backtracking in regex
